title: Dynamic Interleaved Batch-Gap Controller and KV Slice Rebalancer for Mixed-turn Workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our continuous batching scheduler performs well on uniform workloads but degrades when request mixes contain short prompts with long responses and long prompts with short responses. We observe KV cache fragmentation and GPU memory spikes that lead to elevated p99 latency and occasional OOMs under bursty traffic. Goal: Reduce p99 latency and p50 while preserving or improving throughput on mixed-turn workloads by adapting interleaving behavior and reclaiming KV slabs without introducing high tail latency. Approach: 1) Introduce a Batch-Gap Controller that dynamically adjusts the inter-arrival gap tolerance per slot. The controller uses quantile estimates of incoming request decode lengths (from request metadata + lightweight early-token predictor) to allow short requests to interleave ahead of long-running decodes while avoiding busy-waiting that increases latency. 2) Add a KV Slice Rebalancer background compactor that runs on low-util intervals to coalesce underutilized KV slabs across streams and free contiguous GPU memory for large allocations. 3) Add a GPU Occupancy Estimator and admission control hook that rejects or reroutes requests expected to cause OOM to compatible model variants or idle GPU pools. Expected outcomes: 6-12% p99 latency reduction for mixed workloads, 10% better throughput for skewed short-turn bursts, and reduced KV fragmentation/OOM incidence.
acceptance_criteria: Canary run stable for 48h with no increase in error rate or token-level correctness regressions
p99 latency reduced by >=5% on mixed-turn synthetic workload vs baseline (runtime-1.24) under same QPS
Throughput (tokens/s) improved or equal for >=95% of measured traffic slices
KV fragmentation metric (free slab fragments) reduced by >=15% during steady-state
Feature flags exist to disable Batch-Gap Controller or Rebalancer independently
Documentation + telemetry dashboard updated with new metrics and alert thresholds
design_notes: Batch-Gap Controller decisions are driven by a combination of: per-client moving 75th/95th percentile decode length histograms, early-token predictor (first 8 tokens) and a per-slot congestion signal
We use a quantile sketch (DDSketch) retained per 30s window to avoid heavy memory/messaging overhead
Interleaving policy: short-over-long preemption is allowed only if estimated extra wait for long request < per-customer latency-SLO budget fraction

KV Slice Rebalancer operates as a low-priority background stream with epochal compaction - it marks candidate slabs, copies live KV segments to target slabs and releases old slabs; compaction paused if GPU occupancy > 80%
Admission control uses a conservative occupancy estimator; we avoid hard rejections for premium customers and instead route to fallback model variants
We prefer soft handoffs (fallback routing) over queuing when occupancy is tight to preserve customer SLAs
experiments: Perf harness: mixed-turn workload generator v3 (convinced by product) — 60/40 short/long dialogs, mean short=8 tokens, mean long=512 tokens
Test matrix: llama-2-13B q8 on a100, phi-3-micro on p4d; baseline = runtime-1.24 with continuous-batcher v2
Result snapshot (canary run 2026-03-04): p99 latency down 7.2% on a100, throughput +11% on phi-3 under bursty short-turn scenario
KV fragmentation metric decreased 18% across runs where rebalancer activated during low-util epochs
OOMs in synthetic stress reduced from 3/week to 0 in 72h canary for the test fleet
Edge-case: some long-decode tails show +3% p50 due to extra preemption accounting — mitigated by per-customer SLO caps in policy

Stage 2: Canary (10% of shared-host pools) with strict telemetry for 72h - start 2026-03-08 (in progress)
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 50% with 6h checkpoints and automated rollback on p99 increase >3%
Stage 4: Global rollout with customer opt-in for early access; dedicated pools for enterprise clients
risks: Compaction copy could increase transient GPU memory pressure if multiple rebalancers run concurrently - mitigated by staggered epochs and occupancy checks
Early-token predict may misclassify long decodes as short causing tail spikes — kept conservative thresholds and SLO caps
Rollback complexity: reverting partial KV compaction state must be safe; we implement idempotent slab marking and two-phase release
Potential for subtle correctness regressions if rebalancer copies stale KV segments — strict versioning + checksum validation will be added
User-facing latency regressions for latency-sensitive customers if admission control misroutes — route to fallback model variants as safer default
